title: Live control-room seam
description: Objective: connect authenticated daemon commands, bounded queries, typed session coordination, and resumable cursor events to the canonical control room. Deliverable: daemon HTTP/stream adapters, generated client bindings, and control-room data adapters. NOT in scope: client-side transition inference, MCP, JetBrains, graph fan-out, or legacy import. Hard dependencies: Projection outbox core, Bootstrap application services, External effect supervisor, Independent review flow, Crash reconciliation services, Session coordination fabric, and Foundation control-room shell. Owned paths: apps/daemon/src/http/**, generated client package paths, and apps/control-room/src/data/**. Verification: pnpm typecheck && pnpm test.
definitionOfDone: Authentication, distribution compatibility, input bounds, command idempotency, and stable errors are enforced at the adapter boundary.
Cursor gaps and stale snapshots are explicit; one verified snapshot resumes without skipped events.
The client never computes transitions or truth strength and session/terminal messages cannot bypass command authority.
taskRails: Follow the pinned design; this task cannot create authority beyond its named contract.
Fail closed with stable codes and immutable deterministic outputs.
Keep production modules focused, target <=250 lines, split before 400.
Use TDD and stage only explicit owned paths; no worktree, broad add, push, or merge.

implementationPlan.description: Pin the seam and settle the package edge. Confirm on disk that apps/daemon/src/http/ and apps/control-room/src/data/ do not exist (this task creates both). Re-read the committed surfaces this seam exposes: packages/store/src/subscriptions/subscription-contracts.ts (SubscriptionPage and its CURSOR_GAP arm, SubscriptionCursor, SubscriptionGapCause, GenerationBaseline, SNAPSHOT_SUBSCRIBER_PREFIX, SubscriptionCode/SubscriptionLayer) and subscription-read-page.ts / subscription-writes.ts; packages/control-room-client/src/index.ts (createCompatGate) and its generated client plus the existing client-compat, generated-coverage and generator-determinism tests; and apps/daemon/src/index.ts for the established ingress pattern. THEN CHECK apps/daemon/package.json — it declared only @moe/contracts and @moe/scheduler, but sibling tasks in this batch may already have added @moe/store, @moe/core or @moe/runner. Exposing subscriptions needs @moe/store: if it is already there, add nothing; if genuinely missing, request the ownership amendment in #governors citing the precedent approved for child 3, and WAIT. Write down the command registry shape the adapter will be generic over — that genericity is what makes this task independent of its five unbuilt dependencies.
implementationPlan.note:
VERIFIED ON DISK.
(1) apps/daemon/src/http/ ABSENT, apps/control-room/src/data/ ABSENT — this task creates both. No collision.
(2) apps/daemon/package.json ALREADY declares @moe/store (plus @moe/contracts, @moe/core, @moe/scheduler). A sibling task added it. NO ownership amendment needed; no #governors request sent.
(3) BLOCKER FOUND AND ROUTED AROUND: @moe/store does NOT export the subscription surface. packages/store/src/index.ts is 46 lines and re-exports only sqlite-event-store.js; package.json exports map is {".": "./src/index.ts"} only, and moduleResolution is NodeNext, so a deep import of src/subscriptions/* is unresolvable. packages/store is NOT an owned path, so event-stream.ts will be STRUCTURALLY GENERIC over a subscription port — exactly the precedent the store set for itself (SubscriptionEventSource: "depends on the page shape rather than on the store class"). Store refusal code+layer pass through VERBATIM as opaque pass-through fields rather than a re-declared union: a copied union can drift, a pass-through cannot.
(4) createCompatGate is UNREACHABLE from the daemon: apps/daemon does not depend on @moe/control-room-client, and AGENTS.md pins dependency direction toward contracts, so daemon->control-room-client is backwards. Resolution preserving "one compatibility rule, not two": the daemon pin is composed from the SAME authority the client gate uses — RUNTIME_COMMAND_ENVELOPE_VERSION / RUNTIME_QUERY_ENVELOPE_VERSION / RUNTIME_ERROR_REGISTRY_VERSION in @moe/contracts. generated-coverage.test.ts already asserts GENERATED_CONTRACT_PINS equals those live constants, so both sides are provably pinned to one source.
(5) decodeRuntimeCommandEnvelopeBytes ALREADY EXISTS in @moe/contracts and composes decodeBoundedJsonBytes (1MiB body / depth 64 / 256KiB string) + schemaVersion + exact-key check, mapping to INPUT_LIMIT_EXCEEDED / SCHEMA_VERSION_UNSUPPORTED / INPUT_INVALID. The adapter CONSUMES it; it does not re-implement bounds.
(6) Stable error vocabulary is a SUBSET of RUNTIME_ERROR_CODES (AUTHENTICATION_FAILED 401, CAPABILITY_DENIED 403, DISTRIBUTION_MISMATCH, INPUT_INVALID, INPUT_LIMIT_EXCEEDED, SCHEMA_VERSION_UNSUPPORTED, IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT, STORAGE_DEGRADED) with transport httpStatus already in the registry. No invented codes.
(7) Idempotency vocabulary is real: CommandDecisionResponse.disposition "DECIDED"|"REPLAYED", CommandDecisionKey {commandId, principalId, projectId}. Port is modelled on that shape.
(8) sessionCredential lives INSIDE the body, so auth-before-decode is only possible if the adapter takes the credential from the TRANSPORT header. Request shape carries credential + protocolVersion as pre-decode header fields; raw body stays undecoded bytes until after auth.
(9) COMMAND REGISTRY SHAPE (the genericity that makes this task independent of its 5 unbuilt deps): entry = { kind: RuntimeCommandKind, requiredCapability: string, payloadKeys: readonly string[] (exact-shape allow-list), handler }. Registry is a frozen map; boundary code never names a specific command.
(10) INGRESS ORDER settled: authenticate -> protocol pin -> bounded envelope decode -> registry lookup -> authorize (capability) -> payload exact shape -> durable decision (idempotent) -> dispatch. Authorize precedes payload-shape so an unauthorized caller learns nothing about payload shape; no target lookup ever happens before authorization, so no refusal leaks target existence.
(11) GATE SCOPE HAZARD: root vitest.config.ts include is ["packages/**/*.test.ts","tests/**/*.test.ts"] — `pnpm test` DOES NOT DISCOVER apps/**. AGENTS.md says so explicitly. So the named verification `pnpm typecheck && pnpm test` will not run this task's own tests; app-scoped runs (pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test, pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test) must be run and reported as additional evidence.
(12) Generator is a pure function of the @moe/contracts registry (canonicalSurface()), emitGeneratedClient is exported, and generated-coverage.test.ts pins a golden SHA256 of the output. Generated header honesty boundary #5 explicitly refuses to generate an event-stream frame vocabulary. Step 7 will regenerate and confirm byte-identical rather than invent contract surface in a package this task does not own.

implementationPlan.description: Define the adapter boundary vocabulary. Create apps/daemon/src/http/http-contract.ts as exported frozen data: the stable wire error-code list (DoD 1's 'stable errors' means a closed, versioned vocabulary, not ad-hoc strings); the input bound constants for body bytes, field count and depth, reusing @moe/contracts' bounded-JSON limits rather than inventing new ones; the pinned wire protocol version literal used for distribution compatibility; the auth outcome lattice with AUTHENTICATED, UNAUTHENTICATED and UNAUTHORIZED as distinct verdicts; and the COMMAND REGISTRY type — an entry names a command kind, its exact-shape key list, and its handler, so commands from tasks that do not exist yet can be added later without touching boundary code. Data and types only. This registry indirection is the mechanism that makes the rest of this plan buildable while five dependencies are unbuilt, so keep boundary logic strictly free of any specific command's knowledge.
implementationPlan.note:
Created apps/daemon/src/http/http-contract.ts (222 lines, under the 250 target). pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck exit 0.

Contents, all exported frozen data or types:
- HTTP_BOUNDARY_ERROR_CODES: closed 6-code wire vocabulary (AUTHENTICATION_FAILED, CAPABILITY_DENIED, DISTRIBUTION_MISMATCH, INPUT_INVALID, INPUT_LIMIT_EXCEEDED, SCHEMA_VERSION_UNSUPPORTED). Every entry is a RuntimeErrorCode; the exported conditional type BoundaryCodesAreRuntimeCodes resolves to `never` and breaks typecheck if one drifts out of the registry. No second error language was minted.
- HTTP_REFUSAL_STAGES: AUTHENTICATE, COMPATIBILITY, DECODE, REGISTRY, AUTHORIZE, PAYLOAD_SHAPE, DISPATCH — epic rail 6's "which layer refused" is a field, not a comment.
- HTTP_INPUT_BOUNDS: maxBodyBytes/maxDepth/maxStringUtf8Bytes are MAX_JSON_BODY_BYTES / MAX_JSON_DEPTH / MAX_JSON_STRING_UTF8_BYTES verbatim from @moe/contracts, so the seam cannot disagree with the bounded decoder. MAX_COMMAND_PAYLOAD_FIELDS (64) is ADDITIVE and documented as such: the contract bounds body size and nesting but never key count, so a flat payload of a million one-character keys clears every contract limit today.
- WIRE_PROTOCOL_VERSION: DERIVED, never hand-typed — `${RUNTIME_COMMAND_ENVELOPE_VERSION}+${RUNTIME_QUERY_ENVELOPE_VERSION}+${RUNTIME_ERROR_REGISTRY_VERSION}` as const. The doc comment records why this is not a second compatibility rule: createCompatGate pins the same three values via GENERATED_CONTRACT_PINS, and generated-coverage.test.ts already asserts those pins equal these live constants, so both ends derive from one authority. It also records why the gate cannot simply be imported (apps/daemon has no @moe/control-room-client dependency and AGENTS.md points dependency direction toward contracts).
- Auth lattice: AuthVerdict keeps AUTHENTICATED / UNAUTHENTICATED / UNAUTHORIZED distinct. Authenticator.authenticate takes the TRANSPORT credential, never a body field — the envelope's own sessionCredential is unreadable before decode, which is exactly why auth-before-decode is possible at all.
- PortRefusal { code, detail, httpStatus, layer }: verbatim pass-through for port refusals. The seam holds NO translation table, so a store SubscriptionCode/layer cannot be flattened into a generic boundary code on the way out.
- CommandDecisionPort.decide(key, requestDigest, commit): contract states a replay returns the same terminal decision and MUST NOT run commit twice — that is what makes idempotency observable by STATE, since a double write and a correct replay produce identical responses.
- CommandRegistryEntry { kind, requiredCapability, payloadKeys, handler } + CommandRegistry (ReadonlyMap) + buildCommandRegistry. This is the indirection that keeps the boundary independent of the five unbuilt dependency seams; no boundary type names any specific command.
- HttpCommandRequest keeps body RAW/undecoded and carries credential + protocolVersion out of band.

Deviation noted: buildCommandRegistry is a function, and the step said "data and types only". It is a pure data constructor (freezes entries into a Map) that holds no boundary logic and no knowledge of any specific command, so it stays here rather than leaking registry construction into the adapter.

implementationPlan.description: TDD red for the adapter boundary — DoD 1, all five properties. Create apps/daemon/src/http/http-adapter.test.ts before the module, driving a small registry of committed and deliberately synthetic command entries so the boundary is tested independently of any real command. Assert: an unauthenticated request is refused with its stable code BEFORE the body is decoded, and an unauthorized one is refused distinctly from unauthenticated, with neither refusal leaking whether the target exists; a request whose wire protocol version is incompatible is refused through the existing createCompatGate rather than a second compatibility rule; a body exceeding the byte, field-count or depth bound is refused with the specific bound's code, tested AT the boundary (exactly at the limit admits, one over refuses); an unknown command kind is refused rather than ignored; and the error vocabulary is asserted by SET EQUALITY against the exported list so an ad-hoc error string cannot appear unnoticed. Red.
implementationPlan.note:
RED CONFIRMED. `npx vitest run --root . --config package.json src/http` in apps/daemon: "Test Files 1 failed (1)", failure is `Error: Cannot find module './http-adapter.js'` — the module under test does not exist. Correct red reason, not a typo.

Wrote apps/daemon/src/http/http-adapter.test.ts (16 tests) plus apps/daemon/src/http/http-test-fixtures.ts (inputs only; no fixture re-implements a boundary rule, so no assertion runs against a helper that reimplements the production surface). Added CommandAdapterDeps to http-contract.ts.

Registry under test is deliberately mixed: one REAL RuntimeCommandKind ("goal.create") registered, and a second real-but-UNREGISTERED kind ("goal.cancel") used to drive the unknown-kind path — so the boundary is exercised without depending on any of the five unbuilt command seams.

Ordering is probed, not assumed. The unauthenticated tests hand in bodies that a decoder WOULD refuse with a DIFFERENT code: UNDECODABLE_BODY (invalid UTF-8) and a body one byte over MAX_JSON_BODY_BYTES. If decode ever runs before authenticate, the observed code flips to INPUT_INVALID / INPUT_LIMIT_EXCEEDED and the test reddens. The same probe covers compatibility-before-decode.

Distinct refusals: CAPABILITY_DENIED at stage AUTHORIZE / 403 versus AUTHENTICATION_FAILED at stage AUTHENTICATE / 401, asserted as different codes, and handler call count 0 on both.

No target-existence leak: the same refusal is driven with an existing and a nonexistent targetAggregateId and the two whole results are asserted deeply EQUAL, for both the unauthorized and the unauthenticated path.

Bounds tested AT the boundary, admit and refuse both:
- body bytes: envelopeOfExactByteLength builds a valid envelope whose UTF-8 length is EXACTLY MAX_JSON_BODY_BYTES (asserted with expect(atLimit.length).toBe(MAX_JSON_BODY_BYTES)) — admitted; +1 byte refused INPUT_LIMIT_EXCEEDED at stage DECODE with details.limitName "JSON_BODY_BYTES".
- depth: MAX_JSON_DEPTH-2 payload containers admitted (envelope + payload are containers 1 and 2), one more refused with details.limitName "JSON_DEPTH".
- payload fields: exactly MAX_COMMAND_PAYLOAD_FIELDS admitted, one more refused at stage PAYLOAD_SHAPE with details.limitName "COMMAND_PAYLOAD_FIELDS".

Unknown kind refused INPUT_INVALID at stage REGISTRY with handler call count 0 — refused, not ignored. Same for an empty registry, and for a payload carrying an unlisted key (refused, never trimmed).

Vocabulary asserted by SET EQUALITY in BOTH directions: six probes drive six distinct refusal paths, the sweep asserts probes.length === 6 (so a silently empty sweep cannot pass), every probe is asserted to actually be REFUSED, and the sorted observed code set is compared to sorted HTTP_BOUNDARY_ERROR_CODES. A declared-but-unreachable code fails one direction; an ad-hoc string fails the other.

Idempotency tests written now rather than in step 4 so step 4 is pure green: replay asserts SAME effectId/resultCode, disposition DECIDED then REPLAYED, AND port.effects.length === 1 AND handler.calls.count === 1 — the state assertion is what distinguishes a correct replay from a double write. A second test asserts the decision key is built from the AUTHENTICATED principal (principalId/projectId) rather than from body fields. A third asserts a port refusal passes through with the port's OWN code and layer ("IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT" / "DURABLE_DECISION"), proving the seam holds no translation table.

Also asserted: every result is frozen, and a refusal never echoes the presented credential.

implementationPlan.description: Implement apps/daemon/src/http/http-adapter.ts to green, and prove idempotency by STATE. Follow the daemon's established ingress order exactly and do not reorder it: authenticate, then compatibility-gate, then bounded-decode via decodeBoundedJsonBytes, then exact-shape check against the registry entry's frozen key list, then dispatch. Authentication precedes decoding so an unauthenticated caller cannot make the daemon parse attacker-controlled bytes. Command idempotency routes through the store's durable command decision so a replay returns the SAME terminal decision — and assert it by state, not by response: replay a command and check both that the decision matches and that NO second durable effect exists, since 'it did not error the second time' is exactly what a double-write also looks like. Refusals are frozen, carry a stable code, and never echo credentials or reveal target existence. Target under 250 lines; split before 400.
implementationPlan.note:
GREEN. `npx vitest run --root . --config package.json src/http` in apps/daemon: "Test Files 1 passed (1) / Tests 17 passed (17)". `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck` exit 0.

Created apps/daemon/src/http/http-adapter.ts, 177 lines (target <=250). http-contract.ts is 229.

Ingress order implemented exactly as planned and documented in the module header as load-bearing, not stylistic: authenticate -> compatibility -> decodeRuntimeCommandEnvelopeBytes -> registry lookup -> authorize -> payload exact shape -> durable decision -> dispatch. The header states WHY authentication is first: the envelope's own sessionCredential is only readable after decoding, so any other order makes the daemon parse attacker-controlled bytes for a caller it has not identified.

Bounds are NOT re-implemented. decodeRuntimeCommandEnvelopeBytes already composes decodeBoundedJsonBytes, so body bytes / depth / string bytes / duplicate keys / number range all arrive as INPUT_LIMIT_EXCEEDED or INPUT_INVALID from the contract, and the seam surfaces them at stage DECODE. Only the payload FIELD-COUNT bound is the seam's own, because @moe/contracts has no key-count limit.

checkPayload orders field-count before the allow-list so the two rules cannot mask each other and the reason code always names the rule that actually fired.

Idempotency: the seam never calls entry.handler directly. It hands the handler to CommandDecisionPort.decide as a commit thunk, so "no second durable effect on replay" holds structurally — the seam has no other path to the handler. Tests assert it by STATE (port.effects.length === 1, handler.calls.count === 1) alongside the same-decision assertion, plus disposition DECIDED then REPLAYED. The decision key is built from the AUTHENTICATED principal's principalId/projectId, never from body fields.

DISTRIBUTION_MISMATCH needed real care and is documented in the source: that code declares a PROJECT lifecycle source, and createRuntimeError fails closed to UNKNOWN_ERROR without one. The seam refuses before reading any project state, so claiming a source would invent daemon truth. The error is therefore built by projecting lookupRuntimeError("DISTRIBUTION_MISMATCH") VERBATIM for retryability/recoveryCategory/recoveryCommands/transport, with truthClass OBSERVED because the seam itself compared the two pinned versions. This mirrors exactly what client-compat.ts decided on the control-room side, so both ends of the seam refuse the same way for the same stated reason.

Refusals: every result is Object.freeze'd, httpStatus comes from the registry row's transport binding (401/403/400/413/422) rather than a hand-written status table, refusal values are module constants with no request-derived content (so no target-existence leak is even constructible), and no credential is ever echoed. Port refusals pass through with the port's own code and layer verbatim; the seam holds no translation table.

implementationPlan.description: TDD red for resumable cursor events — DoD 2, the correctness-critical path. Create apps/daemon/src/http/event-stream.test.ts. The store already distinguishes these cases; this seam must SURFACE that distinction rather than flatten it. Assert: a normal read returns a PAGE arm carrying nextCursor; a gap returns the CURSOR_GAP arm carrying a digest-verified snapshot, with the gap CAUSE preserved rather than collapsed to a generic 'gap'; and a stale snapshot is refused with its stable code rather than silently accepted. Then the property the whole DoD turns on: resuming from ONE verified snapshot skips NO events — assert it by comparing the union of events delivered across a gap-then-resume sequence against a single uninterrupted read of the same ledger, asserting exact equality of the delivered event id sequence, not merely equal counts. Also assert that a resume with a cursor from a superseded generation is refused rather than silently reseated. Red.
implementationPlan.note:
RED CONFIRMED. `npx vitest run --root . --config package.json src/http/event-stream`: "Test Files 1 failed (1)", `Error: Cannot find module './event-stream.js'`. Correct red reason.

Wrote apps/daemon/src/http/event-stream.test.ts (14 tests), event-stream-contract.ts (wire + port vocabulary), event-stream-fixtures.ts (a ledger-backed port double).

Why a structural PORT and not an import: packages/store does not re-export the subscription surface from its entry point and its exports map has only ".", so a deep import is unresolvable under NodeNext, and packages/store is not an owned path. The port types mirror the store's arms exactly, and a real SubscriptionPageResult is assignable to StreamReadResult unchanged. This is the precedent the store set for itself with SubscriptionEventSource.

Arm discipline asserted structurally, not by comment: Object.hasOwn(gap, "nextCursor") === false, Object.hasOwn(gap, "events") === false, Object.hasOwn(page, "snapshot") === false, Object.hasOwn(page, "cause") === false. Flattening the union into one optional-field object reddens this test.

Gap CAUSE preserved, not collapsed: HISTORY_PRUNED and GENERATION_CHANGED are each asserted by exact value and asserted to differ from each other, so a seam that mapped both to a generic "gap" fails.

Stale snapshot: asserted with the STORE's own code and layer (SUBSCRIPTION_SNAPSHOT_STALE / STATE), never merely "refused". A companion test asserts the forwarded layer is NOT "SEAM", so a locally invented code cannot pass.

Layer attribution: the seam raises only three closed codes of its own (EVENT_STREAM_CURSOR_NOT_ISSUED, EVENT_STREAM_GENERATION_SUPERSEDED, EVENT_STREAM_LIMIT_INVALID) and stamps layer "SEAM"; everything else is forwarded verbatim with the port's layer. Every refusal test asserts BOTH code and layer, so "which layer refused" is pinned.

DESIGN CORRECTION made while writing the test, worth recording: my first draft had resumeFromSnapshot call the port's reseat and then compare generations. That is wrong — reseatToSnapshot does a compare-and-set on the durable cursor, so refusing afterwards would have ALREADY silently reseated, which is the exact failure the plan asked to prevent. The seam now PROBES with the non-mutating readPage first, compares the presented cursor against the gap snapshot's (generation, checkpoint), and only calls reseat once the check passes. The superseded test therefore asserts by STATE: port.reseats() === 0.

Bound: page limit is MAX_EVENT_PAGE_SIZE, which is the store's own MAX_PAGE_SIZE re-exported rather than a second number. Tested at the boundary — MAX_EVENT_PAGE_SIZE admits, +1 refuses, 0 refuses.

The gapless-resume property: the ORACLE IS THE RAW LEDGER, not a second call through the same seam. Comparing the seam against itself would pass even if the seam dropped the same events on both paths. The test drives gap -> resume -> read, then asserts [...ledgerIdsUpTo(snapshot.checkpoint), ...deliveredAfterResume] equals the full ledger id list by EXACT SEQUENCE, and asserts both halves are non-empty so the comparison cannot pass vacuously with one side empty.

Also asserted: no bigint reaches the wire (checkpoint and globalPosition are strings; JSON.stringify does not throw), and every frame plus the events array is frozen.

implementationPlan.description: Implement apps/daemon/src/http/event-stream.ts to green. It exposes the committed subscription surface over the wire and adds NO new gap semantics of its own: readSubscriptionPage supplies the PAGE and CURSOR_GAP arms, reseatToSnapshot performs the reseat, and this module's job is transport, bounds and shape. Preserve the arm discipline the store deliberately built — nextCursor exists only on PAGE and snapshot only on CURSOR_GAP — so a client cannot read a cursor off a gap response and resume from a position that was never delivered; do not flatten the union into one optional-field object, which would undo that guarantee at the boundary. Page sizes are bounded by the adapter's limits. Every refusal carries the store's own SubscriptionCode and layer verbatim rather than a locally invented code, so a reviewer can still see which layer refused. Target under 250 lines.
implementationPlan.note:
GREEN. `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck` exit 0. `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`: "Test Files 8 passed (8) / Tests 128 passed (128)" — the whole daemon package, not just this seam, so nothing existing regressed.

Created apps/daemon/src/http/event-stream.ts, 182 lines (target <=250). event-stream-contract.ts 177, event-stream-fixtures.ts 111.

The module adds NO gap semantics. The port decides PAGE vs CURSOR_GAP vs REFUSED; this module encodes that answer for the wire or refuses on a bound the port does not own. encode() is a three-way switch over the port's arms with no branch that can turn one arm into another.

Arm discipline is structural, not conventional: pageFrame builds an object literal with nextCursor and no snapshot; gapFrame builds one with snapshot and no nextCursor. There is no shared optional-field builder, so flattening the union would require deleting one of the two builders and the Object.hasOwn tests redden.

Transport work that is genuinely this layer's job: the store's bigints (page checkpoint, StoredEvent.globalPosition) are String()-encoded, since a bigint throws in JSON.stringify. Asserted by a test that calls JSON.stringify on a real frame.

Bound: limitRefusal runs BEFORE the port is touched, so an out-of-range page size never reaches storage. Range is 1..MAX_EVENT_PAGE_SIZE, which is the store's own MAX_PAGE_SIZE re-exported rather than a second number.

Refusal attribution: forward() copies a port refusal's code, detail and layer verbatim — there is no mapping table in the file. seamRefusal() stamps layer "SEAM" on the three codes the seam owns. Both paths are covered by tests that assert the layer, including one asserting a forwarded refusal's layer is NOT "SEAM".

resumeFromSnapshot probes with the non-mutating readPage first and only calls reseat after the presented cursor is confirmed to be the exact (generation, checkpoint) pair the open gap issued. Order matters and is documented in the source: reseat is a compare-and-set on the durable cursor, so any check performed after it would mean the cursor had already moved. Refusals therefore leave reseats() at 0, which the tests assert by state.

Typecheck caught a real defect vitest could not: the fixtures' STALE constant was typed StreamReadResult and returned from reseat(), where StreamGap is not assignable to StreamSeatResult. Narrowed to StreamRefused. Worth noting that the green suite was green with that type error present.

implementationPlan.description: Regenerate the client bindings through the EXISTING generator — do not hand-edit generated output. packages/control-room-client already ships generator-determinism.test.ts and generated-coverage.test.ts, which exist precisely to police this; a hand edit will fail them for a confusing reason and waste a debugging cycle. Regenerate so the bindings cover the new command and event-stream surface, then confirm the determinism test still passes (regenerating twice produces byte-identical output) and the coverage test still passes (every exposed surface has a binding). If the generator itself needs a change to cover the new surface, that is a real change to make — but make it in the generator and regenerate, never in its output. Keep createCompatGate as the single compatibility rule shared by client and adapter.

implementationPlan.description: Control-room data adapters — DoD 3, and the ban that must be structural. Create apps/control-room/src/data/data-adapter.ts and data-adapter.test.ts. ADVERSARIAL SELF-REVIEW FOUND THREE REAL GAPS. All three were fixed TDD (red first), and all three fixes were then mutation-drilled.

1. UNCHECKED INDEX ON A MAPPED TYPE. `client.commands[kind]` / `client.queries[kind]` are mapped types over a finite key union, so `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` adds no `| undefined` and TypeScript cannot stop a caller reaching the layer through a cast. The result would have been a raw TypeError instead of a stable refusal. Both now guard `typeof build !== "function"` and refuse INPUT_INVALID without contacting the transport.
2. UNBOUNDED MAP OVER A NETWORK PAYLOAD. `response.payload.map(toViewRecord)` had no length bound, so one oversized response could allocate without limit. Added MAX_VIEW_RECORDS (1000) with a boundary test: exactly the limit admits, one more refuses INPUT_LIMIT_EXCEEDED. The daemon is the trust anchor for truth, but that is not a reason for the receiving side to be unbounded.
3. SILENT DUPLICATE REGISTRATION. buildCommandRegistry let a later entry overwrite an earlier one, so a duplicate registration could silently replace a stricter requiredCapability with a laxer one and leave no trace. It now throws naming the kind; registry construction is startup code, so failing loudly there is the safe direction.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
(1) WHY THIS IS NOT BLOCKED DESPITE SEVEN DEPENDENCIES, FIVE OF THEM UNBUILT. The promotion note said report_blocked would be the correct outcome. It is not, and the reason is that this task's DoD is about the ADAPTER BOUNDARY, not about the commands that cross it. Read the four DoD items: authentication, distribution compatibility, input bounds, idempotency and stable errors (DoD 1); cursor gaps, stale snapshots and resume without skipped events (DoD 2); the client never computing transitions or truth strength (DoD 3); repo gates green (DoD 4). Every one of those is a property OF THE SEAM. None requires any particular command to exist. So the design is: make the adapter GENERIC OVER A COMMAND REGISTRY, and let the unbuilt dependencies contribute registry entries later without touching the boundary code. The boundary is testable today with a small set of committed commands plus deliberately synthetic registry entries.
(2) DoD 2 IS ALREADY BUILT AND COMMITTED. Cursor gaps, verified snapshots and gapless resume are exactly what `packages/store/src/subscriptions/` shipped in task-7617c00d — SubscriptionPage, CURSOR_GAP with a digest-verified snapshot, SubscriptionGapCause, readSubscriptionPage, reseatToSnapshot. This task must EXPOSE that surface over the wire, not reinvent it. That is the single largest reason this task is far more buildable than its dependency list suggests.
(3) DoD 3 IS A NEGATIVE PROPERTY AND NEEDS A STRUCTURAL TEST. 'The client never computes transitions or truth strength' cannot be proven by behaviour alone. Prove it the way the lease core proved its import ban (`mem:task-task-967769ea801f4fe09944e4fdcc47663e-handoff` decision 6): a STATIC SOURCE SCAN over apps/control-room/src/data/** asserting no transition/strength computation and asserting the scanned file list equals an expected set, so a NEW file cannot escape the ban.
(4) GENERATED BINDINGS ARE GENERATED. packages/control-room-client already has a generator with determinism and coverage tests. Regenerate through the existing generator and let its own tests police it; do not hand-edit generated output.
